title: Insulation Rebates in Langley 2026: Up to $5,500 from BC Hydro
desc: Langley covers a Township with new owner-occupied homes and a City that is 61% apartments. BC Hydro's insulation formula, who qualifies, and installers ranked by Google reviews.
lead: Langley is two municipalities with different housing. The Township is mostly owned houses and the City is mostly apartments. That split decides whether the home insulation rebate fits you.
cards_heading: What BC Hydro pays for insulation in Langley
cards_intro: Both the City and the Township of Langley use the same BC Hydro rules. We re-read the insulation page on October 2, 2026. The rebate is for homes heated mainly by electricity, with FortisBC covering the same formula for its gas customers.

cards.title: Attic
cards.amount: $0.02 x R added x sq ft
cards.note: Capped at $900, with at least R12 added.

cards.title: Walls and basement
cards.amount: $0.09 x R added x sq ft
cards.note: Capped at $1,200 each for wall cavity, sheathing and basement or crawlspace.

cards.title: Floors and other spots
cards.amount: $0.07 x R added x sq ft
cards.note: Capped at $1,000, at least R20 added.

cards.title: More than one upgrade
cards.note: A bonus is available when you finish more than one eligible upgrade.

cards.title: Lower incomes
cards.note: Income-qualified customers can get free upgrades.

after_cards:
A Township rancher

A 1,300 square foot attic at R-24 topped to R-50 adds R-26. The rebate is 0.02 x 26 x 1,300 = $676. Insulating 1,000 square feet of exposed crawlspace floor with R-20 would earn 0.07 x 20 x 1,000 = $1,400, so the $1,000 cap applies. That makes $1,676 from our arithmetic on the posted rules.
sections:
In the 2021 Census, the Township of Langley had 46,925 households and the City of Langley had 12,600, together 59,525. In the Township, 23% of households live in homes built before 1981 and 82% own their home, with only 10% in apartments. In the City, 38% live in older homes but 61% are in apartments. Across both, about 15,705 households (26%) live in pre-1981 homes, and 8,405 are owner-occupied houses from that era.

If you are in a City of Langley apartment or condo, the Home Renovation Rebate does not apply. BC Hydro runs a separate Condo and Apartment Rebate Program. The strongest fit is a Township house, especially a rancher or split-level from the 1960s to 1980s.
Rural lots, outbuildings and the 12-month rule

Parts of the Township are farm and acreage land. The program covers the house, not garages, workshops or outbuildings. The home must also be at least 12 months old and a year-round primary residence. A vacation cabin does not qualify.

Langley's average January low from 2015 to 2024 was 0.3°C and the coldest day was -16.8°C. Winters are mild and wet, so savings come from fewer cold weeks, not a long deep freeze. The rebate still covers part of the cost of an attic top-up.

• A Home Performance Contractor Network member must install the insulation.
  • Pests and moisture have to be fixed before the new insulation goes in.
  • Work required for a permitted addition does not qualify.
  • Applications are due within six months of the invoice date.
claim_steps: Check that your Langley home is electric-heated, at least 12 months old and a primary residence.
Get quotes that list the R-value added and the area for each space.
Ask about the bonus if you are also planning another eligible upgrade.
faq: I live in the City of Langley in a condo. Does this apply?
No. Condo and apartment buildings are not eligible for the Home Renovation Rebate. BC Hydro has a separate program for them.
Does my Township acreage house qualify?
The house can, if it is electric-heated and at least 12 months old. Outbuildings and workshops do not.
The average January low from 2015 to 2024 was 0.3°C and the coldest day was -16.8°C.
Can I apply if the account is in my landlord's name?
The account holder must apply or sign a consent form.
Do I need a special installer?
Yes. Insulation must be done by a Home Performance Contractor Network member.
